values.label: Under 15 minutes
values.definition: Expected to finish in fewer than fifteen minutes.

values.label: 25–45 minutes
values.definition: A single-session feature expected to finish in twenty-five to forty-five minutes.

values.label: Low energy
values.definition: Designed for a low-energy player state.

values.label: Medium energy
values.definition: Invites sustained attention and several meaningful conversational responses.

values.label: No movement
values.definition: Can be played without changing physical position.

values.label: Stay nearby
values.definition: May use ordinary nearby details while the player stays in one safe place.

values.label: Grounded noticing
values.definition: The player responds to ordinary details they actually notice.

values.label: Collaborative clues
values.definition: Player and agent separate real observations from harmless fictional clues.

values.label: Branching story
values.definition: Player choices materially change a bounded fictional arc.

values.label: Curious
values.definition: Invites gentle curiosity without claims of certainty.

values.label: Playful
values.definition: Uses light fictional play rather than serious real-world claims.

values.label: Imaginative
values.definition: Centres collaborative fiction and creative choices.

values.label: Romantic
values.definition: Makes fictional affection and courtship part of the authored dramatic question.

values.label: Socially tense
values.definition: Uses public expectation and relationship pressure without physical danger.

values.label: Nearby setting
values.definition: Uses only an ordinary setting already around the player.

values.label: Conversation only
values.definition: The complete activity happens in the current conversation.

values.label: A hard boundary
values.definition: The player may state or decline a content boundary before play.

values.label: Free-text choices
values.definition: The player supplies short choices in their own words.

values.label: Changes each play
values.definition: Different safe observations or choices can shape a new bounded run.

values.label: High authored replay
values.definition: Authored alternate scenes, crisis affordances, and ending families support substantively different replays.

values.label: Authored replay
values.definition: A compact authored story offers alternate routes and endings without feature-length complexity.

values.label: Clearly fictional framing
values.definition: Fiction remains distinct from real-world claims, diagnosis, or recovered memory.

values.label: Fictional romance
values.definition: Adult fictional courtship and optional mutual affection are defining story elements.

values.label: Social pressure
values.definition: The story includes family expectation, public assumption, and reputation stakes.

values.label: Creature threat
values.definition: The fictional story includes coordinated animal threat and comic peril without graphic injury.

values.label: Moderate tension
values.definition: The fictional story sustains genre tension without graphic harm or extreme distress.

values.label: Romance
values.definition: A fictional relationship story in which mutual affection may shape the ending.

values.label: Historical-inspired
values.definition: Uses an original period-inspired social setting rather than a real historical account.

values.label: Science fiction
values.definition: Uses speculative technology, space, or future consequences in an original fictional setting.

values.label: Creature horror
values.definition: Builds tension around an organised non-human threat while preserving meaningful nonviolent choices.

values.label: Western
values.definition: Uses an original frontier setting, civic scarcity, and public reputation without requiring gunplay.

values.label: Haunted horror
values.definition: Uses impossible spaces, apparitions, and restrained supernatural dread without graphic harm.

values.label: Heist
values.definition: Centres a coordinated crew, alternate specialist routes, and the consequences of what they uncover.

values.label: High fantasy
values.definition: Uses an original secondary world, magic, and mythic obligations.

values.label: Mystery
values.definition: Presents a fixed fair-play fictional truth through authored clues and alternate investigation routes.

values.label: Cyberpunk noir
values.definition: Explores personal agency and ownership in an original high-technology urban setting.

values.label: Folk horror
values.definition: Builds unease through inherited ritual, landscape, and community memory without graphic harm.

values.label: Agency
values.definition: Centres who gets to define the meaning of a consequential choice.

values.label: Public truth
values.definition: Explores the cost of correcting a public story that others have already accepted.

values.label: One extraordinary evening
values.definition: The complete dramatic arc unfolds during one bounded social event.

values.label: Ensemble cast
values.definition: A narrator performs several recurring characters with different knowledge and goals.

values.label: Speak in character
values.definition: The player may answer and address fictional characters naturally.

values.label: Describe actions
values.definition: The player may state what their fictional character does.

values.label: Make decisions
values.definition: The player may state or select a consequential course of action.

values.label: Hybrid choices
values.definition: Optional authored approaches support but do not restrict natural free-text responses.

values.label: Moderate emotion
values.definition: Contains sustained relationship and social stakes without extreme distress.

values.label: Gentle emotion
values.definition: Offers a complete consequence-bearing arc without sustained distress or high-pressure conflict.

values.label: Medium reading
values.definition: Uses several short scenes and conversations with a moderate reading load.

values.label: Low reading
values.definition: Uses a few compact turns designed for a short complete session.

values.label: Single session
values.definition: Designed to begin and complete in one conversation without an external save.

values.label: Can be played seated
values.definition: No standing or travel is required.

values.label: General alpha audience
values.definition: First-party personal alpha testing under the published terms.

values.label: English
values.definition: Published and reviewed in English.
